$description:
Shared control contracts.

Component recipes consume these first and introduce component-specific
variables only for genuinely unique needs. Design language overrides the
sizing/feedback tokens (see contracts/environment.css); recipes never hardcode
sizes. Radius comes from the semantic ramp (theme/personalization), not here.

xs.$description:
Height ramp (xs..xl) — web defaults (desktop density: 24/28/32/36/40, to
   match production @atom63/ui). iOS overrides in environment.css.

Recipes resolve rendered size at their own use-site:
  max(calc(height * density), size-appropriate min-SIZE)
Do not cache that formula in a :root custom property. Input, density, and
design-language axes can be scoped to nested providers; deriving at :root
would freeze the root values and ignore those local overrides.

Floor with --a63-control-min-size (rendered geometry), NOT
--a63-control-min-target (interaction). The two are separate on purpose —
see contracts/environment.css. Touch therefore keeps the xs/sm/md ramp
intact and satisfies the 44px target by expanding the interaction area:
compact markers (checkbox, radio, switch, slider, badge) via a positioned
pseudo-element, button-class controls the same way. Square icon buttons are
NOT an exception — they sit on the rendered ramp like everything else, so a
32px icon button and a 32px text button line up in the same toolbar row.

The button recipe delivers that interaction floor on `::before`. Consumer
CSS must not paint on, resize, or hide `.a63-Button::before`: it wins the
cascade at higher specificity than a single consumer class, and silently
breaks either the visual or the touch target.
Inline padding ramp
Icon geometry follows control size, not the compressed text ramp.

$root.$description:
`0 0 #0000` not `none` — composed into comma-separated box-shadow lists
   alongside the focus ring, where `none` invalidates the declaration.

flat.$description:
Shadow for flat/bordered variants (outline, destructive-outline). Defaults to
   the regular shadow; a theme can soften it — e.g. aqua drops the bright top rim
   that's too strong on a light fill while keeping a gentle lift.

tint.$description:
How strongly a control's drop shadow is tinted by its own fill colour (0% =
   neutral shadow). The recipe composes the tinted layer at the button so it
   follows each button's colour; a theme just sets the strength.

xs.$description:
Row block padding. Rows (Item today; Menu/Command rows are the intended
   next tenants) take their height from content + this padding, floored by the
   control ramp, so a single-line row lands on ~44pt and a two-line row on
   ~59pt. Those targets come from our own measurement of shipping iOS apps
   (docs/design-system/web-ios-token-parity.md) — Apple publishes no iOS row
   height, so do not cite UIKit cell metrics for them. It lives here rather
   than in the recipe
   because the design-language axis has to retune it (contracts/environment.css)
   and axes own tokens; recipes only read them.
